Cheap robots.txt preflight check before you call the Minifetch /extract and /run/seo-page-audit endpoints: returns whether Minifetch may fetch a target URL (allow/deny) plus its crawl-delay. If blocked and the site is not yours try our external proxy routes. If blocked and the site is yours or to set a custom crawl-delay read https://minifetch.com/tutorials/unblock-minifetch Checks the URL as given — does not follow redirects. Supports GET & POST

fresh.description: Optional. If true, bypasses the 24h robots.txt cache and re-fetches robots.txt for this check. Use after editing your robots.txt or crawl-delay (or adding/removing a Minifetch block) to confirm the change took effect.

url.description: The target URL to check against robots.txt

allowed.description: Whether the minifetch user agent may fetch this URL per robots.txt

crawlDelay.description: Crawl-delay (seconds) for the minifetch UA; omitted when blocked or the domain is invalid

message.description: e.g. 'Access allowed by robots.txt', 'URL is blocked by robots.txt', or 'robots.txt not found, defaulting to allowed'

minifetchCache.description: robots.txt cache state (~24h TTL; pass fresh=true to bypass)

proxy.description: Fetch provenance — always minifetch UA here

url.description: The URL checked, exactly as given — redirects are not followed

tip.description: Present only when allowed=false: how to retry via the external proxy routes, and how site owners can unblock the minifetch user agent

Keyless web search returning ranked title, URL, and snippet for a query — with locale/region targeting, freshness filters (past day, week, month, year), pagination, a news mode that adds publish date and source, and selectable backend engine (auto rotation, or pin Brave, Yahoo, or Yandex).

engine.description: search backend: auto (recommended - rotates engines and falls back on blocks) or pin one of yahoo, yandex (web mode); news mode supports bing. when set, each result carries an 'engine' field; if the pinned engine returns nothing, auto serves instead and results also carry 'requestedEngine'

mode.description: web results or recent news (news adds date+source per item). the news index is narrow, so a long or highly specific news query that matches nothing falls through to web rather than returning empty; those items carry requestedMode=news and servedBy=web
